page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-lssd-metal is a bare-metal server instance configured with 288 vCPUs across 144 physical Intel Xeon 6985P-C cores operating at 4.2 GHz. The system features 2232 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 7.75 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of six NVMe SSDs totaling 16242 GB. The processor architecture is x86_64, utilizing a 504 MB L3 cache and supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions).

Benchmark data places this server in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 313266.86 and a PassMark CPU score of 178741.62. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 23041.86 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 1090.21 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a top-tier PassMark database score of 39491.44 and Redis SET operations processing 422.06 million operations per second.

Despite the high-density compute and memory configuration, certain workloads show performance limitations. While LLM prompt processing for a medium 7B model is in the top tier at 299.84 tokens per second, text generation for a small 135M model falls into the bottom 10% at 41.9 tokens per second, indicating a bottleneck in sequential text generation tasks without GPU acceleration. This bare-metal instance is optimized for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data compilation, high-throughput web serving, and cryptographic operations.
